transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-30
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Veridian CTO), Carlos Ruiz (Head of ML), Elaine Park (Security Lead), Ravi Patel (Platform Eng)

00:00 Jordan Miles: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on this account, big thanks for taking the time, we'll run through our model catalog and how you can pick open models, compare benchmarks and the compatibility matrix.
00:18 Maya Chen: Hi thanks, excited. We're mostly trying to understand cost/latency tradeoffs for a triage assistant and some batch summarization jobs. Also want to confirm we can keep PHI in our VPC.
00:32 Priya Shah: Great, hi I'm Priya, SE. Quick agenda: we'll demo the console's model catalog, show benchmark snippets, talk about compatibility (GPU types, quantization levels, runtime variants), then discuss Optimize recommendations like batching and KV cache. 
00:48 Carlos Ruiz: Quick context from us: triage assistant is low-latency interactive (~200-400ms token p99 target ideally) and a nightly batch summarization of notes that needs throughput and cheaper unit cost. We currently run on A100 nodes on-prem, some H100 on GCP for spikes.
01:10 Liam Ortiz: Noted. Also curious about model sizes you plan to use and whether you want to stay on open models only?
01:20 Maya Chen: Open models only for now, due to regulatory reasons and cost control. We're evaluating Llama-2 variants, Mistral, and some newer opt-style models.
01:33 Priya Shah: Perfect. In Redwood's catalog we tag models with profiles: architecture, typical cost per token, latency baselines on A100/H100, supported quantization (int8, q4, q2) and runtime compatibility (e.g., optimized kernel path vs generic). I'll share a compatibility matrix — shows which model + quantization + runtime gives best latency on each GPU type.
01:58 Carlos Ruiz: How often are those benchmarks updated? Hidden drift with new kernels is a concern.
: There was a small hiccup, transcription artifact here
02:05 Priya Shah: Yeah good question. Benchmarks are updated whenever we onboard a new model or a runtime kernel changes; we also run periodic re-benchmarks monthly for high-use models. We store the raw artifacts in the console and can share the spreadsheet.
02:20 Jordan Miles: I'll drop that spreadsheet and the catalog export after the call.

02:30 Maya Chen: Walk us through an example — say Llama-2-13B quantized to int8 on A100 vs H100, what should we expect?
02:38 Priya Shah: Sure, quick ballpark: Llama-2-13B int8 on A100 with our optimized kernel tends to give ~1.6x slower p50 compared to H100 optimized, p99s differ more, and cost per token can be ~20-30% higher on older hardware for the same quant level. But if you move to q4_0 or q2 variants you may reduce memory and improve throughput, though depending on model architecture some quality regressions can happen.
03:10 Ravi Patel: On the Private side, we need a customer-managed control plane with KMS integration and audit logs. Elaine insists on key control.
03:20 Elaine Park: Yup, must have either HSM or KMS integration and full audit trails, also data residency.
03:27 Priya Shah: We support KMS integrations and our Private deployment option gives customer KMS/HSM control with an audit log export. We'll send the SOC2 and encryption docs. Note: for VPC private deployments there are small extra latency hops for control plane but inference plane stays in your network.
03:46 Carlos Ruiz: If we go Dedicated reserved capacity, does that give us pinned performance?
03:52 Liam Ortiz: Yes, Dedicated is reserved GPU pools; you get predictable throughput and we can size the pool for your p99 targets. We also support autoscaling and burst capacity if you want headroom.
04:10 Maya Chen: For the triage assistant interactive path the p99 target is strict. How do you approach fallbacks if we run out of capacity?
04:20 Priya Shah: We have routing policies — you can set latency-first or cost-first. For critical routes you can set fallback to a smaller but compatible model (e.g., 7B optimized variant) or route to a different region or Dedicated pool. Console allows per-route rules.
04:40 Jordan Miles: Also Redwood Optimize can recommend batching/caching settings that preserve latency while reducing cost — for the triage assistant we usually keep batching small with prefix caching to speed repeated prompts.

05:00 [Demo starts — screen share described]
05:05 Priya Shah: Here is the model catalog view — filters for architecture, size, intended use (chat, completion, embeddings), and quick links to benchmarks. You can click into a model and see compatibility matrix: GPU types (A100/H100/GPU-T4), supported quantizations, recommended runtime (fast-kernel, generic), and measured p50/p95/p99 latencies for sample sequences.
05:35 Priya Shah: For example, Mistral-8B q4_0 on A100 with fast-kernel shows p99 of ~210ms for 256-token seq in our sample harness, cost per token X — it's all annotated with notes about quality tradeoffs.
06:00 Carlos Ruiz: Are the latency numbers from our infra or from Redwood-hosted benches?
06:06 Priya Shah: Baselines are Redwood-run on common cloud instance types; we also include a "Your infra" mode where we can ingest your benchmark results to show side-by-side. For POC we recommend running the same harness on your A100s to get exact p99.
06:25 Maya Chen: That side-by-side would be great.

06:35 Priya Shah: On the compatibility matrix, you'll see columns for model size, quantization support, runtime variant, memory footprint, and recommended hardware. There's also a checkbox for "Verified for Dedicated/Private".
06:50 Ravi Patel: Any gotchas with certain model+quant combos?
06:54 Priya Shah: Yeah, some newer opt-like models don't have optimized kernels yet and so they fall back to slower code paths; similarly, extreme quant (q2) can drop quality unexpectedly on some architectures. We mark those with a caution flag.
07:12 Carlos Ruiz: Bench methodology — are you using real prompt mixes?
07:15 Priya Shah: We use representative workloads: interactive chat traces for latency, long-form decode for throughput, and batching tests for bulk summarization. We capture token distribution, sequence lengths and run across hardware and runtime variants. We'll include the harness config.

07:40 Maya Chen: Let's talk about accuracy — you mentioned quality regressions with quant. How do you tie QA to quant choices?
07:47 Priya Shah: We run automated evals on redwood-evals (prompt sets) and also encourage customers to run their domain prompts. For example, for clinical triage we recommend a small eval set of 200 prompts (blend of edge cases) and verify acceptable metric delta before promoting an aggressive quant profile.
08:10 Elaine Park: Security question: where do logs live, and do you redact PHI?
08:16 Priya Shah: For Hosted, logs pass through Redwood and are retained per your RG (retention) policy; we can redact at ingestion and we can disable retention. For Private, logs stay in your environment and audit trails are delivered to your SIEM. We support field-level redaction and tokenization pipelines.

08:40 Carlos Ruiz: Ok, hypothetical: we pick Llama-2-13B int8 for interactive but worried p99 is off. Would you recommend trying a smaller optimized model instead?
08:50 Priya Shah: Yes, one pattern is to run a 13B for standard flows and for high-SLA routes use a 7B optimized or a quant profile that hits lower p99. Another is to keep a cache layer and fallback rules so you rarely hit cold path. Redwood's routing and prefix KV cache helps a lot there.
09:15 Jordan Miles: Also we can include headroom via Dedicated reservations for peak windows to keep p99 stable.

09:30 [brief cross talk; background noise]
09:42 Carlos Ruiz: On costing — can you show comparative cost estimates for the nightly summarization if we use 13B int8 vs 30B q4?
09:50 Liam Ortiz: We can produce a cost per million tokens estimate; ballpark, 13B int8 on A100 is usually materially cheaper than 30B q4 due to lower GPU memory/compute; we'll run numbers for your observed batch sizes.
10:08 Maya Chen: Timeline: we're aiming for a POC in Q3, pilot in Q4, but need compliance gating in June.
10:18 Elaine Park: We'll need to review SOC2 and encryption docs before greenlighting any onboarding.
10:24 Jordan Miles: We'll send SOC2 + KMS/HSM docs.

10:35 Priya Shah: Demo — here's the benchmarks tab where you can export CSV. You can also upload your own harness results; the console will map them into our compatibility matrix and recommend an optimal model + quantization profile per your SLOs.
10:55 Ravi Patel: Does the console recommend specific kernel/runtime flags?
11:00 Priya Shah: Yes, it recommends runtime (fast-kernel/generic), suggested batch size, kv cache settings and quant profile. It also shows expected p99 and cost delta. Sometimes the suggestion is "disable batch for route X" to hit latency SLO.
11:18 Carlos Ruiz: Any integration with our CI/CD to roll model versions?
11:22 Liam Ortiz: We support rollouts: canary, A/B, and automatic rollback on eval regressions. These are exposed via API and console; you can pin versions per route.

11:40 Maya Chen: A question about vendor lock-in — if we get model artifacts from open checkpoints, can we export them and run elsewhere?
11:47 Priya Shah: If you're on Private, you manage artifacts yourself; for Hosted we serve models but you can request exportable artifacts depending on licenses. For open models it's typically possible, but we'll work through license constraints.
12:05 Elaine Park: Any SOC2 scoping notes: do you have penetration test reports and architecture diagrams?
12:12 Jordan Miles: Yes, we have SOC2 report, infra diagrams, penetration test summary and a compliance pack. We'll put that in the secure share with access controls.

12:28 Carlos Ruiz: Great. For the POC, what's minimal footprint we should try?
12:33 Priya Shah: For triage assistant start with a 7B optimized q4_0 in Dedicated for interactive flows to validate latency, plus one A100 for the nightly summarization with a 13B int8. Then we can scale up if accuracy requires larger models. We'll produce a POC sizing doc.
12:55 Maya Chen: Sounds reasonable. Cost sensitivity is high so please include cost per 10M tokens for each config.
13:03 Liam Ortiz: Will do — bring back cost estimates broken down by inference and infra.

13:15 [Wrapping up]
13:20 Jordan Miles: Quick recap: we'll send model catalog export, compatibility matrix, benchmark spreadsheet, SOC2/encryption docs. Redwood team to run a quick latency vs cost estimate for the triage and batch jobs; schedule POC scoping call for next week (Jordan to propose times). Elaine to share compliance questionnaire.
13:38 Maya Chen: Good, thanks. Any blockers we didn't cover?
13:42 Elaine Park: No, just the SOC2 docs and KMS integration details are gating.
13:47 Jordan Miles: We'll prioritize those. Thanks everyone.
13:52 [Meeting ends]

Notes: transcription includes a few artifacts (speaker overlaps, small mis-heard words). References: catalog export link (shared post-call), benchmark spreadsheet (shared post-call), SOC2 and encryption docs (to be shared via secure link).
